raw.thesis: Narma proposes an "Enterprise Agentic Brain" to tackle the pervasive challenges AI-first companies face in scaling AI automation. The core innovation lies in its three-layered architecture: Observe, Intelligence, and Execution. Instead of building new foundational AI models, Narma focuses on deeply understanding how work happens within an organization (the "Work Graph") through lightweight desktop sensors. This data feeds into an "Intelligence Layer" that identifies employee intent, business value, and "drift" from intended workflows. The "Execution Layer" then automates the generation, deployment, and monitoring of AI agents for high-ROI opportunities, complete with approval gates for control. This venture aims to provide a continuous AI lift by observing work, deciding where AI can intervene, and continuously building agents. Narma positions itself as a complement to existing foundation models, enhancing their utility by providing a critical layer of contextual understanding and automated application within enterprise workflows. It aims to replace the current fragmented and telemetry-poor approaches to AI deployment and ROI measurement with a unified, intelligent system. The founder's goal appears to be a growth startup, given the scope and ambition of "AI automation at scale" and "Continuous AI lift." The venture is currently at the idea stage, with the concept fully articulated but no evidence of a built product or user traction.
raw.product_description: Narma is an "Enterprise Agentic Brain" designed for AI-first companies to see, prove, and deploy AI automation at scale. It features three layers: Observe (desktop sensors for work patterns), Intelligence (detects intent, business value, and workflow drift), and Execution (Agent Factory for automated AI agent generation and deployment). It leverages existing foundation models, focusing on the "Work Graph" to identify AI application opportunities and provide "Continuous AI lift."
